findings.text: The new test file lies outside the reviewed node's declared write paths: FENCE — SCOPE lists only reckon/crew_run_commands.py, the evidence fragment and the figures directory, while the plan's §4 done-when itself names 'the new test'. The worker recorded the discrepancy in its manifest rather than weakening the test to satisfy the audit; the coordinator should widen the node's recorded scope rather than treat the file as an overreach.

_refuse_a_budget_above_the_resume_fence re-implements the bounded check that reckon/crew/node.py:1352-1367 owns inside validate_node — the same parse_duration, the same resolved_time_ceiling comparison and a near-identical refusal — rather than calling that owner as reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:175-182 does. §4 asks the resume door to apply 'the same bounded check and --over-fence rule as dispatch'; this is a parallel copy of the rule. It bites once §3 lands: the resume stores its reason only inside budget_changes on the run, never on node, so a node-level reader of the recorded reason will not see it and the two doors will disagree about the same fence. Fold into the §3 node that owns the bounded check.

assert change['from'] and change['to'] == RAISED_BUDGET checks only that the replaced figure is non-empty; asserting change['from'] == STORED_BUDGET would make the line fail if the change were recorded against a figure the run never held. The neighbouring deadline and reason assertions are independent of the input, so the guard does not rest on this line.

The done-when requires ruff check and ruff format --check to add no findings on the staged paths, and manifest.md:19 asserts both are clean without naming any log; no lint log exists under logs/, so that clause is claimed rather than recorded.
